correctness.rationale: Ordinary Euclidean distance is strictly conditionally negative definite on distinct sites: the displayed Fourier integral is integrable at zero by the zero sum, at infinity by boundedness, and strictly signed by independence of distinct exponentials. This makes signed mass-one energy strictly concave and the gauging solution unique. With positive triangle limbs l_i, substitution of v_i=(1−1/(T l_i))/2, T=∑l_i^−1, gives the stated common potential. For fixed new mass t, solving the original-site projected stationarity equation gives (1−t)v+tq, with the scalar in Dq+r determined by pairing with v. The affine tangent (q−v,1) is a nonzero zero-sum vector; its negative quadratic energy gives Q>0. Differentiating the resulting quadratic gives exactly the stated t and sign, including distinct-site zeros. The potential is coercive and strictly convex because equality along any segment would put all three noncollinear foci on its line. Its level set is the boundary of a bounded convex body with nonempty interior and no boundary segments; it is analytic away from foci since convexity rules out a stationary value above the minimum. Both the interior and open sides of the original triangle lie strictly inside, permitting an open negative region beyond each side. The equilateral witness satisfies the strict radical inequality and all four points are exposed. Up to three distinct sites the direct gauges have nonnegative masses, including collinear triples with a zero middle mass. As a separate exact check, for foci (±1,0),(0,4/3) and fourth site (0,−9/40), rational gauging gives potential 989/840, threshold 25/21, Q=2189/2100 and fourth mass −5/398 in convex position.
residual_risks: The exact rational test is a witness and a quotient check, not an enumeration of configurations. The proof treats all distinct-site inputs and does not assign weights at collisions or guarantee differentiability at a focus.

evidence: The general Euclidean existence/energy equivalence is known. The spherical-rim result includes planar four-site negative mass at an added center inside the hull, and the bipyramid result studies exposed masses in R³, with five sites in the triangular-equator case.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The new claim is neither existence of negative mass at any planar site nor a statement in any dimension. An interior or higher-dimensional witness does not imply the sharp four-site exposed planar configuration.

evidence: The known energy theorem provides a variational objective, and its first variation gives the algebraic start of the sign test. It does not provide positivity of the triangle coefficients, the strictly convex level curve in original coordinates, or the location of negative sites beyond a planar hull edge.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Credit the Schur/first-variation mechanism as standard. The substantive planar result requires combining the strict triangle limbs with the distance potential, controlling its geometry at and away from the vertices, and identifying a convex-position witness and the lower-cardinality obstruction. Those geometric conclusions are not supplied by substituting dimension in an inspected stronger theorem.

evidence: Theorem 5.4 and Corollary 5.5 identify the weighting with Schoenberg circumcenter barycentrics. The staggered-polygon record gives the same kind of sign at exposed sites but on a different, eight-or-more-site family.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: In the Schoenberg embedding the squared distance is the original distance. A sign relative to the face of its simplex is not a sign relative to the original planar triangle's edges. The energy criterion is an equivalent framework, not itself the original-plane three-focus threshold geometry.

evidence: The closest exact exposed threshold in the index is for two staggered n-gons with 2n≥8. The general primary paper illustrates negative masses in larger planar grid approximations. The indexed planar four-site center formula matches cardinality but not exposed status.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: No inspected exact witness or threshold table matches the arbitrary-triangle sign locus or exposed four-point planar minimum. Exact masses on the index's special symmetry families cannot determine the moving-site sign field.
searches: Resultary 76ffed2e37f7 and 73caf481fce7, exact masses and scopes

originality.rationale: The general signed energy, gauging, and circumcenter criterion, and the phenomenon of exposed negative weights itself, are established. The supported increment is the full moving-fourth-site locus in the original Euclidean plane for an arbitrary noncollinear triple, together with the sharp planar four-site exposed witness. The checked related classes either use more sites, have an interior negative site, or are nonplanar. This is a bounded comparison, not proof of priority.
residual_risks: An unindexed equivalent four-point distance-energy construction or planar-locus description remains possible. Same-day indexing is not a determination of ordering.

value.rationale: The result gives a computable geometric sign test for a new site and diagnoses exactly where negative mass can coexist with hull exposure, which a generic signed maximizer statement does not tell a user working in the original plane. The open negative collars beyond every edge show robustness, and the smallest exposed counterexample pinpoints the boundary between universal nonnegativity and possible negativity by cardinality.
residual_risks: The exact geometry only classifies the added mass over noncollinear triples, not all simultaneous sign patterns or other metrics.
